Definition: from αἴθω (to scorch) and ὤψ (the face, from G3700); an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor):--Ethiopian.
BiblicalUsage: Once, for the Ethiopian eunuch — a man of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who had come to Jerusalem to worship and was reading Isaiah on the road home. This study covers only how the name is used in Acts 8 — the man's story is told there, in the one passage that names him.
TheologicalSignificance: One man, one word, and a whole door opens. I believe the Ethiopian's baptism is the proof that Isaiah's promise was for the nations — a foreigner, a eunuch, an outsider by every law of the old covenant, goes home rejoicing as a baptized believer.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
